statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-70183 (GHSA-494h-xx7x-5frh) is an ASP.NET Core security feature bypass in Blazor (Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Authorization): a stale asynchronous authorization result in AuthorizeRouteView can be applied after navigation or an authorization-state change, bypassing the current [Authorize] decision. Microsoft lists the ASP.NET Core 10.0 runtime packs, including linux-musl-x64 and linux-musl-arm64, as affected from 10.0.0 through 10.0.12 and fixed in 10.0.13 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-494h-xx7x-5frh, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/460, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.13/10.0.13.md). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 10 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 264 packages of the twelve published builds (10.0.2-r0, 10.0.3-r0, 10.0.4-r0, 10.0.5-r0, 10.0.6-r0, 10.0.7-r0, 10.0.8-r0, 10.0.9-r0, 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside the nupkg and other zip archives they hold: every build ships Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Authorization.dll at its own .NET version, in the ASP.NET Core shared framework of aspnetcore10-runtime and of the .NET SDK held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap, and in the ASP.NET Core runtime pack and runtime archive held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap, and in the Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Authorization nupkg in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts, plus reference assemblies with no implementation code: 10.0.2 to 10.0.10 in the first nine builds and 10.0.13 or later from 10.0.13-r0 on. The range ends at 10.0.13-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-70183 (GHSA-494h-xx7x-5frh) is an ASP.NET Core security feature bypass issue: in Blazor, a stale asynchronous authorization result in AuthorizeRouteView can be applied after navigation or an authorization-state change, bypassing the current [Authorize] decision. Microsoft lists the ASP.NET Core 8.0 runtime packs, including linux-musl-x64 and linux-musl-arm64, as affected from 8.0.0 through 8.0.31 and fixed in 8.0.32 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-494h-xx7x-5frh, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/460, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.32/8.0.32.md). DHI dotnet8-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 8 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 220 packages of the ten published builds (8.0.23-r0, 8.0.24-r0, 8.0.25-r0, 8.0.26-r0, 8.0.27-r0, 8.0.29-r0, 8.0.31-r0, 8.0.32-r0, 8.0.33-r0 and 8.0.34-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside the nupkg and other zip archives they hold: every build ships Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Authorization.dll at its own .NET version, in the ASP.NET Core shared framework of aspnetcore8-runtime and of the .NET SDK held by dotnet8-runtime-bootstrap, in the ASP.NET Core runtime pack held by dotnet8-runtime-bootstrap, and in the Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Authorization nupkg in dotnet8-runtime-artifacts, plus reference assemblies with no implementation code (including 6.0.2 reference assemblies in source-build reference packages): 8.0.23 to 8.0.31 in the first seven builds and 8.0.32 or later from 8.0.32-r0 on. The range ends at 8.0.32-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-70183 (GHSA-494h-xx7x-5frh) is an ASP.NET Core security feature bypass: a stale asynchronous authorization result in Blazor AuthorizeRouteView can be applied after navigation or an authorization-state change, bypassing the current [Authorize] decision. Microsoft lists the Linux ASP.NET Core runtime packs among the affected packages and fixed .NET 9 in 9.0.21: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/security/advisories/GHSA-494h-xx7x-5frh, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/460, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.21/9.0.21.md. DHI dotnet9-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 9 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 242 packages of the eleven published builds (9.0.12-r0, 9.0.13-r0, 9.0.14-r0, 9.0.15-r0, 9.0.16-r0, 9.0.17-r0, 9.0.18-r0, 9.0.20-r0, 9.0.21-r0, 9.0.22-r0 and 9.0.23-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold: the ASP.NET Core shared framework ships in aspnetcore9-runtime, with further copies in the SDK held by dotnet9-runtime-bootstrap and in ASP.NET Core NuGet packages in dotnet9-runtime-artifacts. AuthorizeRouteView is in Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Authorization.dll. In every build and on both architectures, its implementation copies, in the ASP.NET Core shared framework of aspnetcore9-runtime and of the SDK held by dotnet9-runtime-bootstrap, in the ASP.NET Core runtime pack held by dotnet9-runtime-bootstrap and in the Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Authorization package in dotnet9-runtime-artifacts, carry that build's ASP.NET Core version; its other copies are reference assemblies with no implementation code. In 9.0.12-r0 through 9.0.20-r0 ASP.NET Core is 9.0.12 through 9.0.20, which are affected; from 9.0.21-r0 on, the version is 9.0.21 or later, with Microsoft's fix. The range ends at 9.0.21-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-70183 (GHSA-494h-xx7x-5frh) is an ASP.NET Core security feature bypass in Blazor (Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Authorization): a stale asynchronous authorization result in AuthorizeRouteView can be applied after navigation or an authorization-state change, bypassing the current [Authorize] decision. Microsoft lists the ASP.NET Core 10.0 runtime packs, including linux-x64 and linux-arm64, as affected from 10.0.0 through 10.0.12 and fixed in 10.0.13: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-494h-xx7x-5frh, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/460, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.13/10.0.13.md. The only change to the Components.Authorization sources between the dotnet/dotnet v10.0.112 and v10.0.113 tags is commit 96bfeb58e4196d1f5701abd037db56b35f215c19 on release/10.0.1xx ("Fix async race condition in AuthorizeViewCore"), which changes AuthorizeViewCore.cs outside tests: https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/commit/96bfeb58e4196d1f5701abd037db56b35f215c19. DHI dotnet-sdk-10 for Debian 13 packages Microsoft's .NET 10 SDK for Linux, which includes the .NET runtime and the ASP.NET Core shared framework. We scanned every package built from this source in the DHI Debian repository, 10.0.301-0, 10.0.302-0, 10.0.302-1, 10.0.400-1, 10.0.401-0, 10.0.401-1, 10.0.402-0, 10.0.403-0, 10.0.404-0 and 10.0.404-1, for amd64 and arm64 (the dotnet-sdk-10 and dotnet-sdk-10-oci-config packages; no debug-symbol packages are published), after verifying each against its index checksum and including the files inside the nupkg archives they hold. The dotnet-sdk-10-oci-config packages hold only an image configuration YAML file and a changelog. Every dotnet-sdk-10 build carries one implementation copy of Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Authorization.dll, in the ASP.NET Core shared framework under /usr/lib/dotnet/shared/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App/<version>, and one reference assembly with no implementation code under /usr/lib/dotnet/packs/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Ref/<version>; no other copy is present, including inside the nupkg archives. The shared framework version is 10.0.9 in 10.0.301-0, 10.0.10 in 10.0.302-0 and 10.0.302-1, 10.0.11 in 10.0.400-1, 10.0.12 in 10.0.401-0 and 10.0.401-1, 10.0.13 in 10.0.402-0, 10.0.14 in 10.0.403-0 and 10.0.15 in 10.0.404-0 and 10.0.404-1, the same on both architectures. Every copy records the dotnet/dotnet commit it was built from: the v10.0.109 to v10.0.112 tags in the builds up to 10.0.401-1, and the v10.0.113, v10.0.114 and v10.0.115 tags from 10.0.402-0 on, all three of which contain the fix commit. The range ends at 10.0.402-0 because it is the first published build with the fix.
